## Quarto

Quarto enables you to weave together content and executable code into a finished document. To learn more about Quarto see <https://quarto.org>.

### Load your packages

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(googlesheets4)
library(readxl)
library(dplyr)
library(rstatix)
library(ggpubr)
```

### Import Data

```{r}
SPAD_data_raw <- read_excel("DroughtNet_MCRS_Fall2025.xlsx", 
    sheet = "SPAD")

Size_data_raw <- read_excel("DroughtNet_MCRS_Fall2025.xlsx",
    sheet = "ShrubSize") 

StomCon_data_raw <- read_excel("DroughtNet_MCRS_Fall2025.xlsx", sheet = "StomatalConductance")

DN_Blocks<- read.csv("DN_Blocks.csv")
```

### Summary Table

|  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|
|  | Hypothesis | Analysis | Results |
| SPAD and seed source | There will be a significant difference between seed sources (inland vs coastal) in mean SPAD values. | One-way ANOVA | SPAD values differ significantly between the mesic and xeric seed sources (p = 6.485e-06). **Specifically, the mesic sources have a higher mean SPAD value as previously hypothesized.** |
|  |  |  |  |
| Stomatal Conductance, Species, and Water Treatment | There will be a significant difference between water treatment or species in mean stomatal conductance values. | Two-way ANOVA | **Significant difference in stomatal conductance across species and water treatment (p=0.016)** |
|  |  |  |  |

## Data Cleaning (SPAD)

```{r}

nrow(SPAD_data_raw)

#Too many rows, clean up NAs
SPAD_data <- SPAD_data_raw%>%
  filter(!is.na(SPAD))

#Check categories are correct
unique(SPAD_data$Water_Treatment)
unique(SPAD_data$Seed_Source)
unique(SPAD_data$Species)

#Remove NAs from Seed_source
SPAD_data <- SPAD_data%>%
  filter(!is.na(Seed_Source))


#Select for necessary columns, remove columns filled with NAs (i.e. FLAG and Notes)

SPAD_data <- SPAD_data%>%
  select(Block_Number, Plot_Number, Water_Treatment, Seed_Source, Species, Leaf_Number, SPAD) 


#change characters to numeric
SPAD_data<- SPAD_data%>%
  mutate(SPAD = as.numeric(SPAD))

SPAD_data <- SPAD_data%>%
  filter(SPAD != "NA",
         Block_Number!= "NA", Plot_Number!= "NA", Water_Treatment!= "NA", Seed_Source!= "NA", Species!= "NA", Leaf_Number!= "NA")


summary(SPAD_data$SPAD)
```

```{r}
#Rename columns to match
SPAD_data<- SPAD_data%>%
  rename(Plant_seed_source = Seed_Source)


DN_Blocks<- DN_Blocks%>%
  rename(Plant_seed_source = Plot.Seed.Source)

DN_Blocks<- DN_Blocks%>%
  rename(Plot_seed_source = Plant_seed_source)



DN_Blocks<- DN_Blocks%>%
  rename(Water_Treatment = Plot.Water.Treatment)

DN_Blocks<- DN_Blocks%>%
  rename(Plot_Water_Treatment = Water_Treatment)

#Change BACPIL to M
SPAD_data<- SPAD_data%>%
  mutate(Plant_seed_source = case_when(
    Species == "BACPIL" ~ "M",
    TRUE ~ Plant_seed_source))


#Join DN blocks and SPAD_Data
NewSPAD_Data <- left_join(SPAD_data, DN_Blocks, by = "Plot_Number")
```

```{r visualize}

#full names of mesic and xeric
NewSPAD_Data<- NewSPAD_Data%>%
   mutate(Plant_seed_source = case_when( Plant_seed_source == "M" ~ "Mesic",
          Plant_seed_source == "X" ~ "Xeric"))
   
#Visualize SPAD Data
ggplot(NewSPAD_Data) + 
  aes(x = Plant_seed_source, y = SPAD) + 
  geom_boxplot()
```

```{r summarize}
SPAD_data_summary <- SPAD_data %>%
  group_by(Plant_seed_source)%>%
  dplyr::summarize(mean_SPAD = mean(as.numeric(SPAD), na.rm=TRUE), sd_SPAD = sd(SPAD, na.rm= TRUE), n = n(), se_SPAD = sd_SPAD/sqrt(n)) %>%
  mutate_at(vars(mean_SPAD, sd_SPAD, se_SPAD), .funs = round, 2)

SPAD_data_summary<- SPAD_data_summary%>%
  mutate(mean_SPAD = as.numeric(mean_SPAD))

SPAD_data_summary

SPAD_model <- lm(SPAD ~ Plant_seed_source + Block_Number, data = SPAD_data)

SPAD_model
```

## Data Cleaning (Stomatal Conductance)

```{r}
# View data set
StomCon_data<- StomCon_data_raw%>%
  filter(!is.na(Stomatal_Conductance), Time!= "HH:MM")

```

```{r}
# Clean dataset

StomCon_data <- StomCon_data%>%
  select(Block_Number, Plot_Number, Water_Treatment, Seed_Source, Species, Leaf_Number, Stomatal_Conductance) 

#Rename columns and join with DN blocks
StomCon_data<- StomCon_data%>%
  rename(Plant_seed_source = Seed_Source)

#Change BACPIL to M
StomCon_data<- StomCon_data%>%
  mutate(Plant_seed_source = case_when(
    Species == "BACPIL" ~ "M",
    TRUE ~ Plant_seed_source))

NewStom_Data <- left_join(StomCon_data, DN_Blocks, by = "Plot_Number")

#full names of mesic and xeric
NewStom_Data<- NewStom_Data%>%
   mutate(Plant_seed_source = case_when( Plant_seed_source == "M" ~ "Mesic",
          Plant_seed_source == "X" ~ "Xeric"))

#change stomatal conductance to numeric
NewStom_Data<- NewStom_Data%>%
  mutate(Stomatal_Conductance = as.numeric(Stomatal_Conductance))

#Fix water treatment values: WA, RS, A
unique(NewStom_Data$Water_Treatment)

NewStom_Data<- NewStom_Data%>%
  mutate(Water_Treatment = case_when(
    Water_Treatment == "WS" ~ "WA",
    Water_Treatment == "RA" ~ "RS",
    TRUE ~ Water_Treatment  # Keep other values as is
  ))

unique(NewStom_Data$Water_Treatment)
```

## One-way ANOVA Analysis (SPAD)

Histogram

```{r}


ggplot(NewSPAD_Data) +
  aes(x= SPAD)+
  geom_histogram()+
  facet_wrap(Plant_seed_source~.)+
  ylab("Count")+
  xlab("SPAD Values")

```

Boxplot

Visualize result: mean SPAD potentially higher in mesic than in xeric plants

```{r}
ggplot(NewSPAD_Data) + 
  aes(x = Plant_seed_source, y = SPAD, fill =Plant_seed_source) + 
  geom_boxplot()+
  scale_fill_manual(values= c( "Mesic"="#257335", "Xeric"="#8ABD95"))+
  ylab("SPAD Values")+
  xlab("Seed Source")

```

```{r}
#summarize mean by seed source
SPADNew_data_summary <- NewSPAD_Data %>%
  group_by(Plant_seed_source)%>%
  dplyr::summarize(mean_SPAD = mean(as.numeric(SPAD), na.rm=TRUE), sd_SPAD = sd(SPAD, na.rm= TRUE), n = n(), se_SPAD = sd_SPAD/sqrt(n)) %>%
  mutate_at(vars(mean_SPAD, sd_SPAD, se_SPAD), .funs = round, 2)
SPADNew_data_summary
#plot the relationship
ggplot(SPADNew_data_summary, aes(x= Plant_seed_source, y=mean_SPAD, fill =Plant_seed_source)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.5, color= "#0C2E0F") + 
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin= mean_SPAD- se_SPAD, ymax= mean_SPAD + se_SPAD), width=0.2)+
  scale_fill_manual(values= c( "Mesic"="#257335", "Xeric"="#8ABD95"))+
  theme(legend.title = element_blank())+
  ylab("Mean SPAD Values")+
  xlab("Seed Source")


```

(As seen in data cleaning, the data is not normal so a kruskal-wallis test must be done instead of ANOVA)\
SPAD values differ significantly between the mesic and xeric seed sources (p = 6.485e-06). **Specifically, the mesic sources have a higher mean SPAD value as previously hypothesized.**

```{r}
result <- kruskal.test(SPAD ~ Plant_seed_source, data = NewSPAD_Data)
print(result)

#data table
my_data_frame <- data.frame(
  SPAD= c("Mean SPAD"),
  Mesic = c("28.19"),
  Xeric = c("21.65"),
  df = c("1"),
  P = c("6.485e-06"))

colnames(my_data_frame) [colnames(my_data_frame) == "NULL"] <- " "

print(my_data_frame)

    knitr:: kable(my_data_frame)
```

Kruskal wallis-test to find differences in SPAD within seed sources across water treatment

**Significant difference between mean SPAD values across water treatments within Xeric treatments.**

```{r}
#Mesic not significant p>0.05
Mresult <- kruskal.test(SPAD ~ Water_Treatment + Block_Number, data = M_SPAD)
print(Mresult)

#Xeric significant p-value = 0.001379
Xresult <- kruskal.test(SPAD ~ Water_Treatment + Block_Number, data = X_SPAD)
print(Xresult)


```

Two-way ANOVA for SPAD, water treatment and species

```{r}
model_SPAD_lm <- lm(SPAD ~ Species*Water_Treatment + Block_Number, NewSPAD_Data)
anova(model_SPAD_lm)


model_SPAD_aov <- aov(SPAD ~ Species*Water_Treatment + Block_Number, NewSPAD_Data)
summary(model_SPAD_aov)


TukeyHSD(model_SPAD_aov)
```

Two-way SPAD results:

**Significant difference between SPAD values across species and water treatment (p=0.003).**

Two-way ANOVA for SPAD, water, and seed source

```{r}
model_SPAD_lme <- lm(SPAD ~ Plant_seed_source*Water_Treatment + Block_Number, NewSPAD_Data)
anova(model_SPAD_lme)


model_SPAD_aov2 <- aov(SPAD ~ Plant_seed_source*Water_Treatment, NewSPAD_Data)
summary(model_SPAD_aov2)


TukeyHSD(model_SPAD_aov2)


```

Results table

```{r}
#data table

anova_df <- as.data.frame(summary(model_SPAD_aov2)[[1]])
anova_df

rownames(anova_df) <- c("Seed Source", "Water Treatment", "Seed Source x Water Treatment", "Residuals")

colnames(anova_df) [colnames(anova_df) == "Pr(>F)"] <- "P-Value"

anova_df <- anova_df[-4, ]  

knitr::kable(anova_df, digits = 4)
```

## Two-way ANOVA Analysis (Stomatal Conductance)

Visualize relationship across water treatment and species

```{r}

head(NewStom_Data)

ggplot(NewStom_Data) +
  aes(x = Species, y = Stomatal_Conductance, fill = Water_Treatment) + 
  geom_boxplot()
```

Check assumptions

```{r}

# Build the linear model
model  <- lm(Stomatal_Conductance ~ Species * Water_Treatment + Block_Number, data = NewStom_Data)

plot(model, which = 2)

# Create a QQ plot of residuals
ggqqplot(residuals(model))
```

Homogeneity test

```{r}
plot(model, which = 1)

NewStom_Data %>% rstatix::levene_test(Stomatal_Conductance ~ Species*Water_Treatment + Block_Number)
```

Statistical Test

Results: **Significant difference in stomatal conductance in water treatment as well as among species (p=0.003) and water treatment (p=0.016)**

Significant: SALMEL-BACPIL (0.003), SALMEL-ERIFAS (p=0.00006).

Significant: WA-RS (p=0.006)

```{r}

NewStom_Data
model_stom_lm <- lm(Stomatal_Conductance ~ Species*Water_Treatment + Block_Number, NewStom_Data)
anova(model_stom_lm)


model_stom_aov <- aov(Stomatal_Conductance ~ Species*Water_Treatment + Block_Number, NewStom_Data)
summary(model_stom_aov)


TukeyHSD(model_stom_aov) # does work

#data table

anova2_df <- as.data.frame(summary(model_stom_aov)[[1]])
anova2_df

colnames(anova2_df) [colnames(anova2_df) == "Pr(>F)"] <- "P-Value"

anova2_df <- anova2_df[-5, ]  
anova2_df <- anova2_df[-3, ]
anova2_df
rownames(anova2_df) <- c("Species", "Water Treatment", "Species x Water Treatment")


knitr::kable(anova2_df, digits = 4)
```

Post-Hoc

```{r}
TukeyHSD(model_stom_aov)
```
